page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, paired with 186.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU, aligning with balanced resource allocation standards.

This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage options. Additionally, it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures that compute resources are fully committed to the instance, avoiding performance degradation from shared-core contention.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-48 offers a predictable resource profile for workloads requiring substantial multi-core processing without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators. It is suitable for multi-threaded applications, web serving, enterprise application hosting, and general-purpose backend workloads that require a balanced distribution of compute and memory resources.
